source.title: Towards Explaining the Regularization Effect of Initial Large Learning Rate in Training Neural Networks
source.authors: Yuanzhi Li; Colin Wei; Tengyu Ma

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices and experiment details.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether learning-rate schedule and training-time pattern learning affect held-out natural-image performance, using a constructed patch task rather than the claim versions’ specified interventions or measures.
record.gate_note: The study does not test random-label fitting, width sweeps, convolution versus fully connected models, adaptive optimizers, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Its CIFAR-10 patch experiments and clean-image accuracy results bear on the broader claim about training conditions and the training-to-test gap. Cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study tests learning-rate schedules and pre-activation noise, which none of V1–V8 names. Its theoretical learning-order results and CIFAR-10 accuracies do not test those versions. References to adaptive optimizers, batch size, and sharpness concern prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors prove a learning-order explanation on a constructed distribution, report supporting evidence on artificially modified CIFAR-10, and show that annealed pre-activation noise can mitigate the small-learning-rate penalty theoretically and empirically.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines large versus small initial learning rates and a pre-activation noise mitigation strategy, not the interventions specified in the claim versions. It uses a constructed two-layer-network distribution theoretically and WideResNet16 CIFAR-10 experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Initial learning-rate schedule and pre-activation noise schedule change reported validation accuracy. On patch-modified CIFAR-10, clean and mixed validation results differ by training method.

fits_no_version.finding: On original CIFAR-10, annealed pre-activation noise raises small-initial-learning-rate validation accuracy from 84.93% to 89.65%; large initial learning rate with annealing reaches 90.41%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Annealed pre-activation Gaussian noise can improve generalization with a small initial learning rate on CIFAR-10 without data augmentation.

fits_no_version.finding: On patch-modified CIFAR-10, clean accuracy is 87.61% with large learning rate and annealing, 69.89% with fixed small learning rate, and 81.36% with small learning rate and annealed noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate and noise schedules affect learning order and clean-image accuracy when CIFAR-10 training includes a deliberately constructed class-predictive patch.

fits_no_version.finding: Under its constructed distribution and assumptions, the paper proves a test-error upper bound of O(pκ log(1/ε1)) for large-then-small learning rates and a lower bound of Ω(p) for small learning rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning order can cause different generalization errors between learning-rate schedules even when both attain low training loss.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 experiments report single-trial results for the noise mitigation comparison; no uncertainty estimates are given. The patch task is artificially constructed, and the reported accuracy tables do not give training error, so they do not directly quantify the training-to-test gap.
record.rows_left_out: No additional applicable numeric results beyond the listed rows. Figure 3 reports accuracy curves for clean validation and patch-only images but does not give values in the text; the qualitative statement that small LR picks up the patch quickly is covered in the page excerpt rather than assigned a figure-only row.

untested.parts: No comparison of fitting fixed random labels and natural labels, including their held-out accuracies.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected generalization comparison; the convolutional theoretical extension does not establish their relative performance.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison or optimizer-tuning intervention.
No batch-size comparison, fixed-epoch batch penalty, or recovery of that penalty.
No dropout intervention or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement, correlation with generalization gaps, or ranking against other measures.
No removal of examples selected by memorization influence versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Generalization is the broad topic, but that alone does not link results to V1–V8. Memorizing a class-predictive patch is neither fitting fixed random labels nor identifying memorized training examples by influence. The relevant numerical values match the supplied text; Table 1's learning-rate conditions require correction.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out random-label accuracy is reported.
No width sweep or test-error measurement across widths is reported.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks is reported.
The experiments compare learning-rate schedules for WideResNet16, not adaptive optimizers against SGD or the effects of optimizer tuning.
The study adds pre-activation noise, not dropout, and does not test dropout or weight-decay removal.
No sharpness or other trained-network generalization measure is evaluated.
No training examples are identified by memorization influence and removed.
